comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C54-C55 regarding differential reliance on global cues in ADHD. Both evaluations support these findings, though OpenEval notes the interpretation is somewhat speculative and would benefit from additional validation, while peer reviewers acknowledge this as contributing to mechanistic understanding without direct challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C66-C69 regarding psychometric validation of assessment instruments. Both evaluations support the methodological rigor, with OpenEval noting reliance on cited validation studies and peer reviewers accepting the measurement tools as appropriate without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C70-C77 regarding experimental design and stimuli. Both evaluations support the methodology, with OpenEval noting the fixed task order as a potential limitation and peer reviewers explicitly endorsing the task as 'well controlled' and 'innovative.'

Strong disagreement on claims C23-C27, C39 regarding the specific relationship between local BM processing and social interaction. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical approaches, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, stating 'the data are not strong enough' and noting that 'many of the differences between correlations are not significant' due to small sample sizes.

Agreement on claims C29-C30, C32-C34, C41-C42, C58-C59 regarding the mediating role of perceptual reasoning. Both evaluations support these findings, with OpenEval noting the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation and peer reviewers acknowledging these as part of the study's contributions without raising concerns.

Agreement on claims C19-C22, C38 regarding group differences in BM perception. Both evaluations support these findings, with OpenEval emphasizing converging statistical evidence and appropriate sample sizes, while peer reviewers describe these as 'important and solid findings' that are 'novel' and 'valuable.'

Partial disagreement on claims C28, C31, C35-C37, C40, C52 regarding age-related improvements. OpenEval finds the statistical evidence SUPPORTED with robust analyses, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, expressing concern about 'theoretical assumptions' and noting that statements about local BM processing not improving with age 'may have been made in previous studies, but would appear controversial and not definitive.'

Agreement on claims C60-C62, C64-C65 regarding participant recruitment and inclusion criteria. Both evaluations support these methodological details, with OpenEval noting some measurement heterogeneity between groups and peer reviewers stating 'methods and materials are presented with sufficient detail so the study could be reproduced.'

Both address claim C56 regarding differential relationships between attention and BM processing types. OpenEval supports this finding as consistent with theoretical predictions, while peer reviewers include it among supported findings about 'relationships to indices of social functioning and possible predictors' without raising specific concerns.

OpenEval rates claim C78 (differential age-related improvements across BM processing types within ADHD group) as UNCERTAIN, noting that specific statistical evidence is not fully presented in the main text and requires verification from appendix materials. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates claims C49, C79-C82 (theoretical interpretation linking local BM deficits to social impairment through cascade mechanism) as UNCERTAIN, noting the interpretation is speculative and the cross-sectional design cannot establish the proposed developmental cascade. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates claim C57 (compensatory mechanisms interpretation) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is speculative and not directly tested in the ADHD sample despite being consistent with findings about IQ effects. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
